title: Test a personality label against two ordinary situations

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A preference is what someone tends to choose; skill is what they can perform under stated conditions; an access constraint limits the available mode or opportunity. A personality label cannot substitute for those distinctions.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional Jo says “I am a quiet person.” In a familiar meeting with an agenda Jo speaks twice accurately after preparation. In a new meeting without a readable agenda Jo contributes nothing aloud but later sends an accurate written question. Jo says writing is preferred and that the missing readable agenda was a barrier. No test score or diagnosis is supplied.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Compare a prediction from the label with both records. Separate preference, demonstrated performance and the reported access issue; name a new bounded question to investigate.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A person prefers written feedback but gives a clear spoken explanation when asked in a suitable setting. Is the preference disproved?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: The global prediction “never contributes” fails. Speaking occurred with preparation; writing is a stated preference; unreadable information is a specific barrier. Silence does not establish lack of interest or ability. Partial: identify the exception but ignore access. Incorrect: diagnose from two meetings. Later compare another willingly chosen accessible setting, keeping the prediction modest.
criteria: Preference skill and access are separated
A label is not a diagnosis or destiny

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Preference is not inability. Preserve the successful spoken example and the person’s stated preferred route without forcing future performance in that mode.
criteria: Preference skill and access are separated
